 2026 Midterm Elections 
 Democrats projected to win Senate majority, opening door to LGBTQ legislation
 U.S. Sen-elect Chris Pappas (D-N.H.) is gay 
 Published
 2 hours ago on
 November 3, 2026 
 By
 Joe Reberkenny 
 The Democrats control both the House and the Senate. (Washington Blade photo by Michael Key) 
 The U.S. Senate has flipped to Democratic control.
 Democrats will control of the Senate after flipping the minimum four Republican-held seats, giving the party control of both chambers of Congress and a majority in the legislative branch, according to NBC .
 The Senate, the upper legislative body, holds 100 seats, two for every state, and oversees several important functions of the federal government, including confirming judicial and Cabinet appointments.
 There will now be two openly LGBTQ members of the Senate: freshly elected Chris Pappas of New Hampshire, who is gay, and Tammy Baldwin of Wisconsin, who is a lesbian.
 With greater control over federal legislation, Democrats could have an opportunity to advance measures such as the Equality Act, which would expand federal protections against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.
 During the campaign, President Donald Trump repeatedly referred to South Carolina Democratic Senator -elect Annie Andrews using the anti-transgender slur “Tranny Annie,” while emphasizing culture war issues, including trans participation in sports and gender-affirming care.
 Democrats, meanwhile, have centered their campaigns on the growing affordability crisis as somatic issues, including the Ukrainian-Russian war, Palestinian-Israeli war, and the war in Iran.

 2026 Midterm Elections 
 Democrats poised to flip House, opening door for expanded LGBTQ leadership
 Robert Garcia among potential committee chairs in new Congress 
 Published
 2 hours ago on
 November 3, 2026 
 By
 Joe Reberkenny 
 The Capitol Dome illuminated at night. (Washington Blade photo by Michael Key) 
 The U.S. House of Representatives is projected to flip to Democratic control.
 According to the Associated Press , Democrats are moving toward control of the House after defeating six Republicans in key battleground races.
 While several major questions remain about how Democrats will lead beginning in 2027, their control of the chamber will expand their oversight powers, allowing them to pursue efforts to check an executive branch that has operated with little congressional oversight over the past two years.
 With control of the House and expanded oversight powers, more LGBTQ Democrats could be positioned to take on leadership roles in the new Congress.
 Incumbent Congressman Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) is poised to become chair of the House Oversight Committee, where he would have greater authority to investigate the Trump-Vance administration, subpoena officials and oversee federal agencies.
 Garcia sent out a two word statement following the confirmation of the Democratic Party’s control: “Lawyer up.”
 U.S. Rep. Mark Pocan (D-Wis.) could gain a leadership position on the House Appropriations Committee, which has authority over government funding. Such a position could allow him to put roadblocks in the way of much of the Republican agenda, including many projects Trump has personally spearheaded while in the Oval Office.
 Some political strategists, like those at Newsweek , have said a third Trump impeachment could be on the table. However, convicting President Donald Trump in a Senate trial would require a two-thirds majority, an outcome that remains uncertain.
 These midterm elections have been rife with personal attacks, gerrymandering at the behest of Trump, and heightened political tensions across the country. Republicans have campaigned on the idea that voters are effectively voting for Trump, while also focusing heavily on transgender issues. Meanwhile, many Democrats have pushed back by centering their campaigns on the growing affordability crisis as the war with Iran continues.

 Gov. Abigail Spanberger campaigned for Question 3 
 Published
 4 hours ago on
 November 3, 2026 
 By
 Staff reports 
 (Bigstock photo) 
 Virginia voters on Tuesday approved an amendment to the state constitution that will codify marriage rights for same-sex couples.
 The Associated Press notes the referendum passed by a 56.2-43.8 percent margin with 76 percent of the vote counted.
